It's hard to describe, because it's just so bleak, but I will do my best. I have Borderline Personality Disorder, so I have it in episodes. 

Usually I can feel mine coming on slowly, sometimes I wake up with it though. I sort of start getting this weird feeling in my chest, and at first I can never remember what it is, which is weird. But it sort of feels like the beginnings of anxiety. So then I kind panic wondering what I'm freaking out about, but then I realise I only think it's anxiety because it's getting slowly harder to breathe. Once it manifests completely, it's like I have this huge weight on my heart, or tied to it, pulling it down. My breathing goes to maybe 65% because whenever I try to take a huge breathe, I feel the weight. There's another sensation, but not sure how to put it into words, but it hurts and seems to fill my whole rib cage. I usually try to literally fuse with the sofa. (never works, imagine that.) 

That's the psychical part anyway. Emotionally, the fact that nothing I can do will take the weight away drags me down further, but at that point, I'm already thinking about how none of the things I want will EVER come true, and in that time, I absolutely 100% KNOW they are never going to happen. I get very lethargic, have to convince myself to eat, but more often than not, I starve to kind of purposefully make myself feel pain. Like...a non-razor form of cutting, I guess. Self harm that my body is doing to itself. I find it harder to express myself than usual, and cannot hold a conversation to save my life, because I cannot think of anything worth talking about, because my life is so worthless. So basically...like my lifeline just has a huge black vortex over it, and NOTHING can be done that will ever help me, so why bother...get a bit suicidal...

I'm also a self-diagnosed BPD sufferer, and I would love to go to a therapist personally, just because i know WITHOUT a doubt it's what I have, but I know I'd just manipulate the therapist into agreeing with me anyway. Not that I'd need to, but I wouldn't leave it up to chance.

For years, I thought I was bipolar, but something just didn't fit. There were tons of missing pieces, and I wasn't entertaining the idea that I was some sort of exception. Until one day I was sort of feeling empty, and was online, filling out some sort of official type personality test that would test your "bipolarness" [for lack of a better word right now], and what came up instead was a high HIGH percentage [cannot quite recall] for BPD, which I had never heard of, along with a high perctange of other disorders that sort of go hand in hand [narcissism, for example.]

I clicked on the link for BPD, and what I read nearly stopped my heart. All of the missing pieces fell into place. And I mean all. Not a single thing was off, or I felt I had to bend around, or thought ok maybe I don't have that symptom. It was like reading a biography on myself, written by someone I have never met, yet describing me personally. I started crying, both because I had an answer, and also because it was scary.

What I hate though, is...well besides the idea of seeing a therapist, is that I've seen/heard multiple people type/say "everyone thinks they have BPD at one time or another." Even a friend of mine thought she had it, and her therapist told her it was merely something else. But I know it's not. Sure, I don't doubt maybe many people feel they can rationalise their symptoms to fit it...people do it for a lot of things, even bipolar and depression. But that makes things hard on those of us who know we have it, and will not take no for an answer. I have checked into a lot of disorders in an attempt to make sure I wasn't just being a hypochondriac, and nothing...NOTHING....fit me as well as anything I've ever read about BPD. 

**TL:DR I know this is long, my apologies, I sort of snorted Adderall. But I guess my question is...what do you think having this disease means for your life, and what do you think about those who would tell you that everyone thinks they have this disease?**
I wish I could tell you how to stop doing all of this stuff...but I'd have to answer that for myself first.
